title: Human Traffic of Stadium
prompt: Find all stadium rows that belong to a group of 3 or more consecutive ids where people is at least 100. Return id, visit_date, and people.
expected_query: WITH high_traffic AS (SELECT id, visit_date, people FROM stadium WHERE people >= 100), numbered AS (SELECT id, visit_date, people, id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS group_key FROM high_traffic), valid_groups AS (SELECT group_key FROM numbered GROUP BY group_key HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT id, visit_date, people FROM numbered WHERE group_key IN (SELECT group_key FROM valid_groups);
explanation: Filter to high-traffic rows, create consecutive groups with id - row_number, then keep groups with at least three rows.
hints: Group by id - row_number and require COUNT(*) >= 3.
common_mistakes: Checking consecutive dates after filtering incorrectly.
Counting all stadium rows instead of high-traffic rows.
Returning only group ids instead of the original rows.
